newsitem.title: USA: Rubin-Strong dlr in US interest, no policy change.
newsitem.headline: Rubin-Strong dlr in US interest, no policy change.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Thursday said U.S. policy on the dollar was unchanged and that he feels a strong currency is in the country's interest.
"Our view is that a strong dollar is in our interest," Rubin said in an interview on CNBC. "On the other hand we share Japan's concern expressed last night about the recent movements in the yen."
Rubin added that exchange rates follow fundamentals and noted that the U.S. economy has had strong economic fundamentals for the last four years and that that is being reflected by the U.S. currency.
"Our policy is absolutely unchanged," Rubin said in answer to a question about the dollar and possible confusion in financial markets about U.S. policy.

"I never comment on the direction of the dollar," Rubin said. "But there was no implication in any statement I have made at any point of this with respect to a preferred direction to the dollar up or down."
He said it was important for Japan to provide strong domestic demand-led growth and avoid a significant increase in its current account surplus.
"The challenge for Japan is to figure out how to accomplish that," Rubin said.

He said that a strong deregulation policy "is very much in Japan's interest and in the interest of the rest of the world." He said it will take some time to see the impact on the Japanese economy from a deregulation program.
